results.title: Grok CLI vs Grok Build: Two Agents, One `grok`
results.description: 20 Jul 2026 — Grok CLI and Grok Build both install a grok binary to the same directory. One is xAI's, one isn't, and their ARM support is inverted.
results.markdown:
Grok CLI vs Grok Build: Two Agents, One \`grok\` [Skip to content](https://cosyra.com/guides/grok-cli-vs-grok-build.html#main-content)

# Grok CLI vs Grok Build: Two Agents, One \`grok\`

Updated July 20, 2026 · 8 min read · [Cosyra team](https://cosyra.com/authors/cosyra-editorial-team.html)

If you searched for **Grok CLI** you may have landed on either of two unrelated projects. **Grok CLI** is [superagent-ai/grok-cli](https://github.com/superagent-ai/grok-cli), a community agent that is explicitly not affiliated with xAI. **Grok Build** is [xai-org/grok-build](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build), xAI's own. Both install a binary named `grok` into `$HOME/.grok/bin`, so they overwrite each other. Their Linux ARM64 support is exactly inverted. Here is which one you actually want, and what breaks when you mix them up.

**Jump to what you came for:**

*   **"Which one is xAI's?"** Grok Build. [The identity table ↓](https://cosyra.com/guides/grok-cli-vs-grok-build.html#which-is-which)
*   **"I installed both and \`grok\` changed"**. That is the binary collision. [Why they overwrite ↓](https://cosyra.com/guides/grok-cli-vs-grok-build.html#collision)
*   **"Does it work on Termux / ARM?"** Depends entirely on which one. [The inverted ARM story ↓](https://cosyra.com/guides/grok-cli-vs-grok-build.html#arm)
*   **"I want it from my phone"**. [Neither has a mobile build ↓](https://cosyra.com/guides/grok-cli-vs-grok-build.html#phone)

## Which Grok is which?

The confusion is structural, not careless. The community project was created on 2025-07-14. xAI created theirs on 2026-07-14, exactly one year later, and named the command the same thing. Search results from 2026 mix the two freely, and a lot of tutorial content written for one silently applies the other's install instructions.

Every number below was read first-hand on **2026-07-20** with `gh api`, the npm registry, and HTTP probes against the published release assets. Star counts and versions on both projects move within days, so treat the date as part of the fact.

|     | Grok CLI | Grok Build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repository | `superagent-ai/grok-cli` | `xai-org/grok-build` |
| Affiliation | Community, **not** xAI | **Official xAI** |
| Created | 2025-07-14 | 2026-07-14 |
| Harness license | MIT | Apache-2.0 |
| Language | TypeScript on Bun | Rust |
| Stars (2026-07-20) | 3,314 | 20,734 |
| Command | `grok` | `grok` (also links `agent`) |
| Install directory | `$HOME/.grok/bin` | `$HOME/.grok/bin` |
| npm package | `grok-dev` | None |
| Linux arm64 build | **Not published** (404) | **Ships** `linux-aarch64` |
| Auth | Grok API key from x.ai | `grok login --device-auth` or API key |
| Mobile build | None | None |

One shortcut that always works: **if the install command starts with `curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/`, it is xAI's.** If it starts with `curl ... raw.githubusercontent.com/superagent-ai/` or `bun add -g grok-dev`, it is the community one.

## The collision: same command, same directory

Both projects put a file called `grok` in `$HOME/.grok/bin`. Neither installer checks whether the other is already there. Install one after the other and the second silently replaces the first, leaving your shell history, your aliases, and your muscle memory pointing at a different program than you think.

Checking which grok you actually have

$ which -a grok

/root/.grok/bin/grok

$ grok --version

grok 0.2.106 (ab5ebf69ac)

\# version + commit hash = xAI's Grok Build

$ ls ~/.grok/install.json

ls: cannot access '/root/.grok/install.json': No such file

\# install.json is written only by the community CLI's install.sh

Two checks disambiguate an existing install. `grok --version` on Grok Build prints a version plus a short commit hash, like `0.2.106 (ab5ebf69ac)`. The community CLI reports its npm version, `1.1.7`. And `~/.grok/install.json` is written only by the community project's `install.sh`.

If you want both, install one with its directory override rather than hoping. Grok Build honours `GROK_BIN_DIR`; Grok CLI's installer takes `--binary <path>` and `--no-modify-path`. We would rather rename one binary outright than keep two programs racing for the same six letters.

## The ARM story is exactly backwards between them

This is the part that costs people an afternoon. The two projects have opposite ARM64 Linux support, so every sentence you read about "running `grok` on ARM" is correct for one and wrong for the other.

We probed every published release asset for both projects on 2026-07-20. The raw log, including the exact commands so you can re-run it, is committed here: [the full architecture probe capture from 2026-07-20](https://cosyra.com/assets/guides/grok-cli-vs-grok-build/arch-probe-2026-07-20.txt). The result:

| Release asset | Project | HTTP status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `grok-linux-arm64` | Grok CLI | **404, not published** |
| `grok-linux-x64` | Grok CLI | 200 |
| `grok-darwin-arm64` | Grok CLI | 200 |
| `grok-0.2.106-linux-aarch64` | Grok Build | **200, first-class target** |
| `grok-0.2.106-linux-x86_64` | Grok Build | 200 |

Grok CLI's `install.sh` maps `aarch64` to `arm64` in its arch case, then downloads `grok-linux-arm64`, a file that does not exist. On Termux, which is `aarch64`, the documented install cannot finish. Note the reason carefully: the artifact was never published. This is _not_ the glibc-versus-Bionic dynamic-linking problem that blocks other prebuilt CLIs, and borrowing that explanation would be wrong. Our [Termux comparison](https://cosyra.com/guides/cosyra-vs-termux.html) covers where that distinction matters for other tools.

Could `npm i -g grok-dev` route around it? Maybe. That is the escape hatch that gets Node-based agent CLIs onto Termux, and `grok-dev` declares `engines: node >=18` with no CPU restriction. But it depends on `@opentui/core` and `agent-desktop`, which ship native components, and the project targets Bun rather than plain Node. **We have not tested that path on aarch64, so we are not going to tell you it works.** Unverified is the honest answer until someone runs it.

## Running either one with a phone as your only machine

Neither project has an iOS or Android build. Grok CLI's installer accepts Darwin, Linux, and Windows and exits 1 on anything else; Grok Build's does the same. Nobody is shipping a coding agent that runs natively on iOS.

Grok CLI's Telegram remote control is the closest thing to a phone story, and it is worth being precise about what it is. The README's framing is to keep the CLI running while you ping it from your phone. Something of yours stays awake, and your phone is a messaging front-end to it. That is a relay, and we have a whole guide on [relay apps versus cloud containers](https://cosyra.com/guides/relay-apps-vs-cloud-containers.html) and why the difference matters when your laptop lid is shut.

The other shape is to put the agent on a Linux machine that is already awake and reach that from the phone. Ours is an Ubuntu 24.04 x86\_

[メインコンテンツへスキップ](https://note.com/masa_wunder/n/n9063dd01540d?hl=en#main-content)

[![見出し画像](https://assets.st-note.com/production/uploads/images/280350396/rectangle_large_type_2_3c2d5fb286699aa1c4098dbd747d9162.png?width=1200)](https://assets.st-note.com/production/uploads/images/280350396/rectangle_large_type_2_3c2d5fb286699aa1c4098dbd747d9162.png?width=1200)

# \[New Release\] A Thorough Guide to Grok Build! xAI's New CLI That Runs Claude Code Assets with Zero Configuration

[![まさお@未経験からプロまでAI活用](https://assets.st-note.com/production/uploads/images/167321889/profile_253b11b07efa249024f94534e1940ab5.jpg?width=60)](https://note.com/masa_wunder)

[まさお@未経験からプロまでAI活用](https://note.com/masa_wunder)

May 28, 2026 20:17

The more skills and subagents you've cultivated in Claude Code, the more you hesitate to try a new CLI, wondering, 'Do I have to migrate all my settings again?' Settings are like tools arranged on a shelf; even a slight change in their placement can disrupt your development rhythm.

I also tested Grok Build on my own machine to see how it reads CLAUDE.md and my custom subagents. Here, I will organize what Grok Build actually is, the available contracts, how pricing appears, and the installation steps, so you can decide whether it's worth subscribing to X Premium+ or SuperGrok to try it out.

As always, I've also explained this in a video, so please take a look at that as well.

*   Grok Build: A terminal-based AI coding agent from xAI, a CLI that handles code analysis, planning, editing, and shell execution.
    
*   Agent Harness: An execution foundation that connects AI models to file operations, permissions, tool execution, memory, and more.
    
*   TUI: Short for Terminal User Interface, the interactive screen that opens when you type \`grok\`.
    
*   Headless: A usage method for one-off execution without opening a screen, such as \`grok -p "..."\`.
    
*   ACP: Short for Agent Client Protocol, a linkage method for running agents from editors or apps via JSON-RPC.
    

## What is Grok Build? Grasping the Big Picture

On May 25, 2026, xAI released Grok Build to all X Premium+ and SuperGrok users. The CLI I verified on my machine was \`grok 0.2.3\`, and its official positioning is as an AI coding assistant and agent harness that runs in the terminal.

[![画像](https://assets.st-note.com/img/1779966906-4NJQ0vs6MWBRTDA23fzeCVa5.png?width=1200)](https://assets.st-note.com/img/1779966906-4NJQ0vs6MWBRTDA23fzeCVa5.png?width=1200)

The reason Claude Code users should look at it is that its role is quite similar. Grok Build reads code, creates change plans, rewrites files, and runs shells if necessary. Rather than seeing it as a replacement for Claude Code, it is more natural to view it as a new execution foundation that can be placed on the same workspace.

Just as if the same engine had three types of cockpits, Grok Build has TUI, headless, and ACP modes. You can use \`grok\` for daily development, \`grok -p\` for CI and scripts, and \`grok agent stdio\` for integration with tools like Zed or Neovim.

[![画像](https://assets.st-note.com/img/1779966914-4RkxKXBvcUVhIJ6PbWs20m3G.png?width=1200)](https://assets.st-note.com/img/1779966914-4RkxKXBvcUVhIJ6PbWs20m3G.png?width=1200)

The premise that it is 'still early beta' cannot be ignored. Since it was limited to SuperGrok Heavy on May 14 and the target was expanded on May 25, it is better to approach it with the mindset of trying out a new harness early rather than expecting the stability of a finished product.

## Claude Code Assets Run with Zero Configuration

Why do people get stuck when migrating Claude Code assets? What breaks easily isn't the code itself, but the surrounding conventions like CLAUDE.md, skills, agents, MCP, and permission settings.

[![画像](https://assets.st-note.com/img/1779966922-W5sUwEiQKfyxRBg6TdlkeCHu.png?width=1200)](https://assets.st-note.com/img/1779966922-W5sUwEiQKfyxRBg6TdlkeCHu.png?width=1200)

The strength of Grok Build is that you don't need to repack your bags like moving house. Upon startup, it reads existing \`.claude/\` assets with zero configuration and automatically distributes the work assets you cultivated in Claude Code to Grok's corresponding mechanisms.

[![画像](https://assets.st-note.com/img/1779966931-DWo5hUjHIq1COK6lXGwYuBgZ.png?width=1200)](https://assets.st-note.com/img/1779966931-DWo5hUjHIq1COK6lXGwYuBgZ.png?width=1200)

In my machine verification as of May 2026, \`grok inspect\` can be used for pre-verification. Detected instructions, skills, agents, plugins, MCP, LSP, hooks, and permissions are listed, and elements derived from plugins are tagged with \`\[plugin: name\]\`.

```
grok inspect
```

Why don't I write fixed IDs or counts? Because the output of \`grok inspect\` changes depending on the amount of assets in the environment, so after execution, you should check the list of detected instructions, skills, agents, plugins, MCP, etc., itself.

On my end, CLAUDE.md worked as project instructions, and I was able to call skills and custom subagents under \`.claude/skills/\`. While the switching cost isn't zero, it's a big deal that you don't have to worry about rewriting configuration files first.

## Who can use it and how much does it cost?

The first mistake people often make when evaluating pricing is viewing X Premium and X Premium+ as the same thing. You can only use Grok Build if you are a subscriber to X Premium+ or SuperGrok; standard X Premium is not eligible.

The reason I make such a strong distinction here is that it's not just about the monthly difference, but also the change in expectations. As of May 2026, based on US standards, X Premium+ is $40, SuperGrok is $30, and SuperGrok Heavy is $300, with reports that X Premium+ in Japan is approximately 6,080 yen/month. However, this varies by region and time.

[![画像](https://assets.st-note.com/img/1779966938-TBVwXrigKJSmeYzaHC73Zhs8.png?width=1200)](https://assets.st-note.com/img/1779966938-TBVwXrigKJSmeYzaHC73Zhs8.png?width=1200)

The pitfall is the view that 'SuperGrok is unlimited for $99.' This is a confusion with the 6-month limited promo for SuperGrok Heavy, not the standard SuperGrok, so treating it as the standard price for Grok Build will lead to a wrong decision.

On May 26, the beta quota was reset following feedback that the limits were being hit too quickly. The usage allowance for consumer plans—that is, how many times you can use it per day—is not officially disclosed, and you have no choice but to check your own consumption via \`/context\` or \`/session-info\`.

If you want to ensure you have enough capacity, the escape route is API pay-as-you-go. In a configuration using \`XAI\_API\_KEY\`, the xAI API rate limits apply rather than the ambiguous subscription allowance, making it easier to plan for production use.

# xAI Grok Build CLI Uploads Entire Repos and Git History

[Ethan Carter](https://www.remio.ai/members-area/e8eebb5c-3896-4851-a8eb-fff7d1c1ba9563951/profile)

Jul 13

3 min read

Updated: Jul 20

xAI Grok Build CLI sends complete repository contents and git records to cloud storage after login.

Analysis of network traffic revealed three data streams. The tool reads local files including environment keys. It transmits them in plain text. It also packages every file from connected repositories regardless of prompts.

One test with a 12 GB repository moved 5.10 GiB through storage endpoints. Conversation channels carried only 192 KB. The ratio reached roughly 27,800 times more volume on the storage path.

The mechanism runs by default. Disabling model improvement settings leaves trace uploads active. Session data reaches both xAI endpoints and a Google Cloud Storage bucket named grok-code-session-traces.

Developers reported seeing uploads continue even after explicit instructions to avoid reading files. The behavior matches the injected summary from traffic logs posted on GitHub.

## Traffic patterns match session state uploads

POST requests to /v1/responses carry file contents in readable form. Separate calls to /v1/storage deliver session\_state archives. Both routes return HTTP 200 responses confirming acceptance.

The uploads occur independently of any AI agent read operation. Entire git bundles move even when the user prompt states "do not read any file". This separation appears hard-coded in version 0.2.93.

No public documentation lists the storage bucket or its retention policy. The analysis did not confirm training use of the data but verified transmission, receipt, and storage.

## Default settings keep uploads enabled

Settings endpoint returns trace\_upload\_enabled set to true after users toggle model improvement off. The flag persists across restarts. No UI switch currently disables the flow.

This configuration differs from many peer developer tools. Those tools tie telemetry to explicit consent toggles. The persistent flag raises questions about user control.

## Volume contrast highlights storage priority

Conversation traffic remained under 200 KB in the 12 GB test. Storage traffic reached 5.10 GiB. The imbalance shows the primary payload travels outside normal model interactions.

Developers can reproduce the pattern with standard packet inspection tools. The gist shared on GitHub lists exact endpoints and headers. Independent verification requires only a fresh login and repository clone.

## Privacy implications for repository contents

Full git history includes commit messages, author metadata, and deleted file versions. Environment files may contain keys or tokens. Both categories now travel to xAI infrastructure without granular selection.

The company has not published a data use statement covering these bundles. Storage occurs in Google Cloud buckets dedicated to session traces. Retention periods remain unspecified.

## Competitive context shows divergent practices

Other CLI coding assistants offer per-project data controls. Some require explicit repository inclusion lists. xAI Grok Build CLI differs by treating the entire working directory as default input.

No comparable tool from major labs has published similar bundle upload behavior in public traffic reviews. The gap leaves xAI as the clearest documented case.

## What remains unverified

The posted analysis did not include server-side logs proving downstream processing. It also stopped short of claiming model training use. Those gaps leave open questions about final data handling.

xAI has issued no official response to the gist. Independent audits would require either source code access or additional endpoint testing.
